rationale:
Evidence. The entityR1 candidate (kp 6.0, kd 0.6, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m) is identical to iteration 8, which has already raced and is the best result so far at 123.04. Its feedback was written against iteration 6, so I have not resubmitted it. Iteration 8 results: oval steering_oscillation 0.293, oval max_error 0.0646 (still above the 0.06 off-track limit), line losses 1.4 (oval), 1.3 (s-bend) and 1.0 (slalom), progress 0.57, 0.24 and 0.09. Across kp 7.0, 6.5 and 6.0, oval oscillation rose (0.250, 0.270, 0.293) while max_error stayed at 0.061 to 0.065. So cutting kp has not reduced jitter, and the edge response is what holds max_error near the limit. Body width cannot relax the off-track limit, so control must bring max_error under 0.06.

Change. I widen the sensor array from x = ±0.030 m to x = ±0.040 m (spacing 20 mm, from 15 mm), keeping 16 mm footprints and the same weights. The sensors then see the edge about 10 mm further out, which gives earlier warning before line loss. Because the signal is a normalised weighted average, widening the array by 4/3 reduces the signal per unit offset by about 4/3. I scale kp by the same factor, 6.0 to 8.0, so the effective edge gain stays as in iteration 8. kd stays at 0.6 and the other controller fields are unchanged, so the result isolates the sensing change.

Expected result. Line_loss_events fall below 1.4 on the oval, and oval max_error drops below 0.06 because the robot gets earlier edge information. Steering_oscillation may stay near 0.27 to 0.29, since the effective gain is unchanged.

Risks. The higher raw kp (8.0) may raise oscillation if the sensor-to-signal gain is not as close to 4/3 as assumed. Edge noise may also rise with a wider footprint.

Hypotheses. (1) max_error is limited by sensing reach at the first large offset, not by gain. (2) Oscillation is set by the effective gain and kd, so keeping the effective gain the same should keep it near the current level.

Next steps after the race. If oval max_error is now below 0.06 and line losses fall, keep this geometry and test base_speed 1.6 for progress. If oscillation rises above 0.3 at kp 8.0, return kp toward 7.0 on this geometry. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more at the same bend entries, change line_loss to search_left or search_right, favouring the side the failing bends turn towards.

Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation, max_error, line_loss_events, progress and completion_time per track, plus rms_error and control_effort.
